correspondence.component_scope: chosen southern opening
correspondence.finding: The chosen southern opening lies in the depicted headwater feeder corridor that joins the Avalik drainage. The source depicts a continuous feeder approach; the short southward V in the stored generalized line is not reproduced literally. No separate drainage, divide crossing or intervening waterbody transfer is required to interpret this ordinary corridor correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: headwater feeder and avalik join
correspondence.finding: The south-to-north feeder and the following northwest approach form a connected stream corridor into the repeatedly labeled Avalik River. Neighboring small branches and lakes remain distinct from the selected channel. The selected line simplifies bends and offsets locally from the detailed linework without selecting a different drainage.

correspondence.component_scope: upper avalik turn and middle mainstem
correspondence.finding: Repeated Avalik River labels follow the connected upper and middle river through its westward and northwestward turns. The original source shows the continuous meandering trunk and tributary joins over every selected interval. Nearby lakes do not require an unexplained selected through-lake connection.

correspondence.component_scope: middle to lower avalik wetland corridor
correspondence.finding: Avalik remains continuously depicted through the northwestward reach, the wetland-rich lower corridor and the westward reach past the Avalitkok Creek setting. The selected route follows the mapped trunk through the tributary junctions; wetland symbols surrounding it do not obscure or interrupt the through-channel.

correspondence.component_scope: avalik kaolak junction and kuk transition
correspondence.finding: The source depicts lower Avalik meeting the Kaolak River corridor and the joined river continuing north with Kuk River labels. The Ketik River approach is separately mapped nearby. This connected confluence supports a Kuk receiving-system identity while retaining Avalik as a distinct named upstream reach.

correspondence.component_scope: kuk widened wetland reaches
correspondence.finding: The source continuously maps the northward Kuk River through the wetland plain into widened, island-bearing reaches. All selected joins are within this connected river corridor. Exact island-side channels and current seasonal water levels are outside the naming finding.

correspondence.component_scope: actual stored terminal
correspondence.finding: The actual stored endpoint falls within the mapped widened Kuk River reach, north of the Omalik River entry and south of the Ivisaruk River junction. The finding stops there; it does not extend the selected path to Wainwright Inlet or an open-sea mouth.

correspondence.component_scope: lake glacial and managed passage check
correspondence.finding: The inspected route is a connected stream-and-river corridor with wetland surroundings and widened lower river reaches. Adjacent lakes, including the Takrak Lake setting, are not selected through-lake passages. No selected glacier, reservoir, canal or managed diversion passage is indicated by the source cartography.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual western opening and eastward Elk Canyon approach before the first clearly depicted Piñon Creek channel
correspondence.finding: The selected opening and eastward approach follow the Elk Canyon valley near the Bear Spring and McEwan Spring setting. The focused original shows the canyon, roads, springs and isolated short hydrographic marks, but does not establish the full selected opening-to-creek watercourse connection. This is a specific missing source depiction, not an inference that an arid canyon has no stream.

correspondence.component_scope: Named upper and middle river from the Lick Canyon/Piñon vicinity, eastward bend and southward foot-of-rim reach; excludes the southern tail of part 11
correspondence.finding: Repeated Piñon Creek labels and the depicted intermittent channel follow the selected eastward course near Piñon, its southeastern bend and the southward reach along the western foot of The Rim. The part-to-part joins and approaching tributary settings correspond at ordinary corridor scale. The mapped creek ends before the selected continuation toward Piñon Wash; no surveyed name boundary is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern tail of the mapped creek and selected southeastward transfer to the Piñon Wash corridor
correspondence.finding: The original maps depict the lower Piñon Creek and the northern Piñon Wash as separate channel extents. The selected route continues south and southeast from the former toward the latter across the plain north and east of Hackberry Hill. Neither the overview nor the focused original establishes that intervening selected link. Shared name elements and basin setting are insufficient to fill this interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected middle overlap with the separately labeled Piñon Wash
correspondence.finding: The intermittent watercourse labeled Piñon Wash supplies the selected middle corridor and bends across the County Road G25 setting. Its southern source depiction turns southwest; the stored route subsequently continues farther south across Crow Flats. The mapped wash is supported as a component without extending its label through the remaining plain.

correspondence.component_scope: Departure from the mapped southern wash, Crow Flats plain, first New Mexico playa and transfer toward the Texas basin
correspondence.finding: After the shared wash reach, the selection crosses the broad Crow Flats plain toward the first mapped playa. The focused middle view and terminal view depict roads, small isolated water features and multiple salt-flat/playa areas; they do not depict a continuous selected watercourse or a specified through-connection over the long plain interval. The New Mexico playa and Texas basin settings are visible, but the intervening selected plain/playa transfer is not established. Current wetness, exact banks and operational flow are not required; the missing ordinary through-link remains material.

correspondence.component_scope: Texas salt-basin passage and actual stored terminal; excludes the northern transfer described above
correspondence.finding: The selected southern route follows the mapped Texas playa/basin corridor east of the Dell City farming grid and crosses the Williams Road/Salt Basin Dunes Road setting. Its actual stored endpoint lies within the broad lower salt-flat area labeled Salt Basin. Ordinary basin correspondence is supported for this terminal component; the map does not establish a whole-route river name, a permanent lake, current water level or a river mouth at the earlier creek endpoint.

correspondence.component_scope: Fragment joins, lake/salt-flat/wetland and managed-passage scope
correspondence.finding: All thirty stored parts of the one selected mainstem fragment were considered. The named creek and wash joins are covered where their channels are drawn; the actual missing opening, creek-to-wash, Crow Flats and northern playa connections are retained above. Lower salt-flat/playa settings and road crossings are visible. No selected reservoir or wetland through-route is independently established, and no diversion or irrigation operation is assumed to connect the gaps.

correspondence.component_scope: opening and upper valley
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is in the Cabin Canyon vicinity. The original detail depicts the northwest-running watercourse toward the Beartrap and Gleason canyon setting. The inventory explicitly connects Cabin and Beartrap Canyon waters to Aliso Canyon Creek. Together, the mapped corridor and direct tributary relationships establish the selected upper approach at ordinary scale; the modeled opening is not asserted to be the surveyed source.

correspondence.component_scope: aliso to santa clara join
correspondence.finding: The selected northward valley passage reaches the Santa Clara corridor near Acton. Map labels identify Gleason and Aliso canyons and the receiving Santa Clara River. The inventory identifies Gleason Canyon as an Aliso tributary and Aliso Canyon Creek as a tributary of Santa Clara River Reach 8. This explicit relationship supplies the through-link where the composite map alone does not draw uninterrupted blue linework. It is more specific than shared basin membership.

correspondence.component_scope: acton soledad canyon
correspondence.finding: Below the Aliso approach, the selected route follows the repeatedly labeled Santa Clara River south past Acton, around Ravenna and west through Soledad Canyon. The mapped receiving channels and connected valley trunk cover every intervening selected part, including the Arrastre, Agua Dulce and Sand Canyon settings. The river corridor remains distinct from adjacent roads and railways.

correspondence.component_scope: santa clarita and castaic join
correspondence.finding: The original map follows the selected Santa Clara bend through Santa Clarita and west past the north- and south-side tributary entrances. The county identifies San Francisquito and Castaic among the principal tributaries. Cartography supports their joining the selected trunk, rather than replacing it with a reservoir or a northward tributary route.

correspondence.component_scope: county boundary piru corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected route continues along the broad, repeatedly named Santa Clara channel through the county-boundary valley and past Piru Creek. Lake Piru and the Castaic reservoir setting are depicted to the north on contributing tributaries; neither is a selected through-lake passage. The receiving Piru junction is supported by both original mapping and county hydrologic prose.

correspondence.component_scope: fillmore sespe santa paula
correspondence.finding: The original map depicts the selected westward river below Fillmore, the Sespe Creek entrance and the southwest turn toward Santa Paula. Santa Paula Creek is mapped joining the same trunk. These junctions do not create changes to the representative Santa Clara identity; the selected route remains on the downstream river corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: saticoy and recharge setting
correspondence.finding: Below Santa Paula the selected route follows the mapped Santa Clara through the Saticoy/Oxnard Plain corridor. Original cartography distinguishes the river from nearby managed ponds and channels and carries the river downstream past that setting. County prose explains diversion of a portion of river water to settling and recharge ponds. Ordinary river through-continuity is supported without assigning current diversion operations or an exact weir crossing.

correspondence.component_scope: actual estuarine coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The final selected part reaches the Santa Clara estuary beside McGrath State Beach, south of Ventura Harbor. The detailed original connects the labeled river to the broad coastal lagoon; the selected endpoint lies in that mapped mouth setting. McGrath Lake farther south is a separate waterbody. The surface-water inventory explicitly lists the estuary as tributary to the Pacific Ocean. The generalized coastal terminal is established without claiming an open sandbar or exact current shoreline position.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southeastern opening and first northwestern approach
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies beyond the southern coverage of Figure 1. General Galán headwater prose does not identify this chosen feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern edge connection into the published river corridor
correspondence.finding: The source-edge approach is visible, but its connection back to the chosen opening is not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Long eastern-flank approach
correspondence.finding: Figure 1 depicts the corresponding connected eastern river course.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern bend through the field-study sampling corridor
correspondence.finding: The labeled Los Patos sampling reach follows this northwestern approach.

correspondence.component_scope: Aguas Calientes junction
correspondence.finding: The map shows the western Aguas Calientes tributary joining Los Patos.

correspondence.component_scope: Northbound course toward the salar
correspondence.finding: The connected mapped course continues north from the junction to the salar margin.

correspondence.component_scope: Salar-entry passage
correspondence.finding: The river reaches the mapped salar, but its selected continuation across that surface is not drawn.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern salar loop and westward turn
correspondence.finding: The selected loop crosses the depicted salar setting without a corresponding channel line. General braided-flow prose does not resolve that loop.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern return and actual western terminal
correspondence.finding: The western ending lies within the depicted salar setting; no source establishes its receiving feature or final through-link.
